newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian ministers fly home for cabinet changes.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian ministers fly home for cabinet changes.

text.p: Two Egyptian ministers close to the economic reform programme flew home from abroad late on Monday amid consultations on changes in the cabinet.

Youssef Boutros-Ghali, minister of state for economic affairs, cut short a visit to London, cancelling an engagement at the Royal Institute for International Affairs and a news conference, the government newspaper al-Akhbar said.
Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid came home from the United Arab Emirates, where he was promoting investment in Egyptian industrial and agricultural projects.
Asked if he had cut short his visit because of the cabinet consultations, he smiled broadly and said: "I finished my work in the Emirates, so why should I stay?"
Al-Akhbar said the government had also summoned Mufid Shehab, chancellor of Cairo University, from Kuwait to meet Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri.

Sources close to the government said on Monday that six or seven of the 30 ministers and ministers of state would probably change, mainly among those responsible for public services and aspects of the economy.
Al-Akhbar said the cabinet changes would take place within hours. The rival newspaper al-Ahram said within several days.

Boutros-Ghali, nephew of the former U.N. secretary-general, is a U.S.-educated free-marketeer said to be impatient with the pace of the economic reform programme. A source in his office said he expected to see Ganzouri on Tuesday.
The international Arabic-language newspaper al-Hayat said Boutros-Ghali was tipped to replace Economy Minister Nawal el-Tatawi, one of two women in the current cabinet.
The cabinet changes would be the first since Ganzouri took office in January 1996.
